snippet_highlighted_words: detect the presence of the SARS-CoV-2 virus, which causes the disease

list.snippet: Rapid, on-the-spot tests that detect viral proteins (antigens) in a sample (usually a nasal swab or saliva).
If antigens are present, the test produces a positive result, indicating an active infection.
Less sensitive than PCR tests and may require multiple tests for accurate diagnosis.
Performed in a laboratory and detect viral genetic material (RNA) in a sample.
The RNA is amplified (made into multiple copies) using a process called PCR.
A positive PCR test indicates the presence of the virus, even if the viral load is low.
More sensitive than antigen tests and considered the gold standard for COVID-19 diagnosis.

text_blocks.snippet: Both types of tests require a sample to be collected from the patient, typically a nasal or throat swab. The sample is then analyzed to determine if the virus is present.
